Export engineer, fix pass 7. Start 03:25, last test 04:11, report 04:14 (49 minutes). Only src/js/45-export.js changed; src/css/45-export.css is untouched. The final page dist/r7-export.html builds and the frozen smoke test tools/smoke-v6.json passes on it (42 steps, exit 0, "no console errors", log out/r7/export/smoke.log). Notes: notes/r7-export.md.

export-2 and export-3 are fixed and measured. export-1 is fixed in its two hard parts (the number never goes up, by construction and in every run; the bar now follows the time), but the first number is only roughly right: on the final page it came 25 s into a 112 s job and was twice too long, then came into line (within about a third from half way, within a few seconds over the last third).

How export-1 works now: before any tile is drawn every tile is "felt" (thin strips across and down it, 1/32 of one pass, timed twice, the cheaper reading counts; under half a second for 4K). The bar is the share of that felt cost drawn. The time left is the felt cost still to draw times the pace of the tiles drawn last, with a margin on the long side; no number in the first 5 s nor before two heavy tiles are finished; it is only ever lowered.

Everything was measured on the shared GPU while the other engineers' tests ran (46 Chrome processes at one point): the same 4K Fine job took 47 to 112 s from run to run and single tiles were 2 to 10 times slower in one run than another. I could not measure a quiet machine. Two things I learned that others should know: (1) small 8 x 8 patches do not measure cost (a tile with a thin spike read four times too dear), strips as wide as the job's own pieces do; (2) the page slows its own job right after a change: sceneWarm in 40-render.js was still preparing formulas 20 s after a mode switch, and the same Kleinian 2560 x 1440 job took 4.5 s started at once and 2.4 s started 20 s later.

Not reached: the two optional items (frame gaps at the very end, the step at x = 2048 in the 2D 4K picture) were not worked on; for the first I have a measurement only.

Engineer "mesh", fix pass 7. Started 03:25, last measurement 04:10. What changed in the mesher (src/js/46-mesh.js only): each slice's estimates are turned into distances before marching (new meshTrue: an estimate outside the solid is divided by its own slope against its six neighbours, never shortened, at most four times lengthened; meshBuild now reads one slice ahead). Measured cause on v6: straight up from the Douady rabbit's top the raw estimate rises 0.49 per unit at the surface, 0.25 one cell out and 0.19 from three cells on, so a level counted in that estimate moved the top 1.4 cells for 0.5 asked and 9.1 for 2 asked. Offset 0 gives exactly the v6 surface. A first version broke the Mandelbrot needle at 128 (a true half cell cannot catch a spike running between samples), so samples beside a part thinner than a cell (a "pit" in the estimates) keep the plain estimate; that restored the needle. The starting offset stays 0.5: measured, it is where the 128 model and the picture agree best. Also done as FIX7 asked for mesh-1: a mesh point's colour is now taken between the two ends of its grid edge by its place on the edge.

Measured on real pictures at the default offset: outline overlap with the picture at 128 cells is 0.949 (Mandelbrot), 0.967 (rabbit), 0.956 (Julia c = -1), 0.945 (cut) against 0.883, 0.889, 0.855, 0.889 on v6; at 512 it is 0.927, 0.949, 0.955. Built-in sphere, torus, gyroid, pearl, noise: all closed; sphere still within 0.002 cells of the asked radius at offsets 0, 0.5 and 2.

Measured versus reasoned: everything above was measured. Reasoned only: my own catch branch in meshSave for a saveFile that throws (the new 00-core.js no longer throws, so the test went through its returned failure); that the lost-graphics sentence also covers a loss before the event is delivered (isContextLost on the canvas); the choice of the constants 0.25, 0.5, 0.8, 200.
